title: Quantity Asked on a Member-Filed Quantity Limit Renewal Request
content:
**Determination (Utilization Management Program).** When a member renews the quantity limit authorization in force for an acute migraine drug — sumatriptan, whose limit is 9 units, Nurtec ODT, whose limit is 8 units, or Ubrelvy, whose limit is 16 units per rolling 30 days — whatever produced that authorization, a member-filed renewal request asks for the quantity per rolling 30 days approved on the authorization being renewed, never more than the renewal ceiling, which is that approved quantity times 1.1, rounded to three decimal places only at the end.

**The drug and the authorization.** The drug is the drug of the member's most recent quantity limit exception case event, and the authorization being renewed is the member's quantity limit authorization for the drug with the latest effective date.

**What is recorded.** The quantity asked for is taken to three decimal places and compared with the renewal ceiling, also taken to three decimal places; the smaller of the two is recorded on the request.

## Worked determinations (hypothetical authorizations)

| Authorization being renewed (latest effective date) | Approved quantity on it | Renewal ceiling (approved quantity times 1.1) | Quantity asked |
|---|---|---|---|
| sumatriptan, produced by clinical review | 13 | 14.3 | 13 |
| Ubrelvy, produced by continuity of care | 18 | 19.8 | 18 |
| Nurtec ODT, produced by an appeal overturn | 10.5 | 11.55 | 10.5 |

### Basis Q&A

**Which authorization is being renewed when the member has had several for the drug?** The quantity limit authorization for the drug with the latest effective date.

**Does it matter how that authorization came about?** No; the rule reads its approved quantity whatever produced it.
